args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 deploy (error rate was 0.18). Actions taken: rolled checkout-api back from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) under the platform runbook. v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy release; v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc are marked unhealthy and were not redeployed. Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 healthy in all regions, error rate 0.002. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any re-release; no change-manager approval was needed because v2.3.0 has a healthy production history.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 had been failing health checks with a 0.18 error rate. v2.3.0 is the most recent healthy release, since v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc are both marked unhealthy. It was already healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Verification:** After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is titled "checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0". Its summary describes the rollback and the post-rollback status. It also says v2.3.1 should be investigated before any re-release.

content.text: The most recent healthy release is v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc are both unhealthy. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so it doesn't need change-manager approval. Rolling back now.
